XII.}}</noinclude>desolate: and euery citie or house deuided agaynst it self, shal not stand. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=26}}† And if Satan cast out Satan, he is deuided against him self: hovv then shal his kingdom stand? {{verse|chapter=12|verse=27}}† And if I in Beelzebub cast out deuils: your children in vvhom do they cast out? Therfore they shal be your iudges. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=28}}† But if I in the Spirit of God do cast out deuils, then is the kingdom of God come vpon you. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=29}}† Or hovv can a man enter into the house of the strong, and rifle his vessel, vnles he first binde the strong? and then he vvil rifle his house. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=30}}† He that is ‖ not vvith me, is agaynst me: and he that ‖ gathereth not vvith me, scattereth. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=31}}† Therfore I say to you, euery sinne and blasphemie shal be forgiuen men, but ‖ the blasphemie of the Spirit shal not be forgiuen. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=32}}† And vvhosoeuer shal speake a vvord agaynst the ‖ Sonne of man, it shal be forgiuen him: but he that shal speake against the Holy Ghost, it shal not be forgiuen him neither in this vvorld, ‖ nor in the vvorld to come. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=33}}† Either {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ It is a mans owne free wil and election, to be a good tree or an il tree: to bring forth good fruites or bad. S. Augustine vpon this place. ''li. 2 c. 4 de actis cum Felic. Manichæo''.}}∷ make the tree good, and his fruite good: or make the tree euil, and his fruite euil. for of the fruite the tree is knowē. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=34}}† You vipers broodes, hovv can you speake good things, vvhereas you are euil? for of the aboundance of the hart the mouth speaketh. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=35}}† A good man out of a good treasure bringeth forth good things: and an euil man out of an euil treasure bringeth forth euil things. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=36}}† But I say vnto you, that euery ‖ idle vvord that men shal speake, they shal render an account for it in the day of iudgement. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=37}}† For of thy wordes thou shalt be iustified, and of thy vvordes thou shalt be condemned.

{{verse|chapter=12|verse=38}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=THE GOSPEL vpon vvenesday the first weeke of Lent.}}Then ansvvered him certaine of the Scribes and Pharisees, saying, Maister, vve vvould see a signe from thee. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=39}}† who answered, and said to them,

The vvicked and aduouterous generation seeketh a signe: and a signe shal not be giuen it, but the signe of Ionas the Prophet. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=40}}† For as {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Ion. 2, 2.''}}* Ionas vvas in the vvhales belly three dayes and three nightes: so shal the Sonne of man be in the hart of the earth three dayes and three nightes. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=41}}† The men of Niniuee shal rise in the iudgemēt vvith this generation, and shal condemne it: because {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Ion. 3, 5.''}}* they did penance at the preaching of Ionas. And behold more then Ionas here. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=42}}† The {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''3. Reg. 10, 1.''}}* Queene of the South shal rise in the iudgement vvith this generation, and shal condemne it: because she came from the endes of the earth to heare the vvisedom of Salomō, and behold more<noinclude>{{rh|||then}}</noinclude>
